messages:
sophia_support: fyi — customer 'acme-prod' on a support call seeing sustained 503s from hosted inference streaming endpoints starting ~14:31 UTC. They say responses abruptly cut with gateway 503 and client logs show truncation. Impacting live feature.

kimps: attaching a short excerpt from customer: "streaming disconnected: upstream returned 503" and server side they saw worker exit.

dmitri_runtime: can you paste the worker logs? any CUDA/oom traces?

sophia_support: customer logs + our worker logs: 
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
[run] cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
[runner] CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED at cublasLtCreate
[worker12] signal 6 (ABRT), aborting
```

jamie_infra: correlating infra metrics — GPU memory usage on pool hosted-prod-gpu-1 spikes right before crash. I see batchmap size jumped from 8 -> 16 at 14:32 UTC (dynbatch ramp).

kevin_sre: is this after yesterday's dynbatch change?

dmitri_runtime: yes — the dynbatch change increases allowed batch depth for streaming endpoints. Hypothesis: long-lived streaming sessions + KV/prefix cache growth + larger dynbatches -> resident GPU allocation growth and OOMs. Repro notes: run streaming client with long context (~8k tokens), enable simulated toolcalls that hold contexts open, and ramp to ~150 RPS with batch target 16.

# repro curl (rough):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-stream","stream":true,"input":"<long prompt>"}'

sophia_support: customer used streaming toolcalls with repeated prefix appends, so memory didn't trim. They have screenshots of repeated partial toolcall outputs.

jamie_infra: mitigation steps taken: 1) triggered fallback routing for customers hitting errors -> route to hosted-prod-gpu-2 which runs safe-quant model variant; 2) rolled dynbatch flag back on hosted-prod-gpu-1 (temp) to batch target 8; 3) enabled temporary QPS throttle for this org to limit buildup. auto_deploy_bot: rollback task started.

auto_deploy_bot: Rollback task initiated by jamie_infra on pool hosted-prod-gpu-1 (change-id: rb-172500-A).

kevin_sre: added a short-term circuit-breaker rule to reject requests that keep streaming for >10s of inactivity and to return 429 instead of letting worker retain memory.

dmitri_runtime: planned fixes: A) cap per-session KV cache growth and evict LRU earlier for streaming sessions; B) add defensive allocator check to fail fast with 429 and avoid process abort on memory alloc failure; C) add aggressive OOM handler to return 500+graceful and restart worker cleanly if necessary. Hotfix estimate ~2 hours for patch + rollout to hosted pools.

sophia_support: told customer we've done routing fallback + throttle, they see reduction in errors but asked for ETA on permanent fix. They're satisfied with monitoring update for now.

dmitri_runtime: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and a permanent build to avoid dynbatch x long-stream combos causing OOM.

kevin_sre: note for postmortem: include traffic pattern, batchmap change, streaming session retention times, and exact allocator failure traces.

jamie_infra: will gather kernel logs and nvregdriver dumps and attach.

sophia_support: thanks — I'll keep customer updated and collect any additional client logs. :thumbsup:
